title: Comet and asteroid detection
intro: Find 3I/ATLAS in five telescope images and follow its motion against the stars.
dataset: 3I practice · five FITS exposures of 3I/ATLAS · 120 seconds each · luminance filter.
outcome: Locate 3I/ATLAS and the main-belt asteroid (90) Antiope, inspect their measured positions, and save a still image or a blink animation.

steps.title: Open the moving-object workspace
steps.requires: Citizen Astronomy is installed and its launcher is open.
actions: Under **Detect & Measure**, click **Asteroid / Comet Detection**. If a different workspace is already open, choose **Mode** and select **Asteroid/Comet Detection**.
steps.check: The workspace shows an **Open** button and an empty object table. Start with five images for a short practice run, or use one image for a catalogue check.
steps.alt: The Asteroid / Comet Detection card is outlined in the middle of the launcher.

steps.title: Unpack the five practice frames
steps.requires: Download the **3I/ATLAS practice set** above.
actions: Extract the ZIP in your Downloads folder. Open **3I practice** and sort the files by **Name**.
Check for the five files ending in **0001_c.fits** through **0005_c.fits**. These are the five exposures outlined in the screenshot. Keep them together.
steps.check: Your practice folder contains five FITS files, all beginning **Light_3I_120.0s_Bin1_L**. Their numbers run from 0001 through 0005.
steps.alt: File browser sorted by Name with the first five original 3I FITS filenames selected and outlined.

steps.title: Find the observing-site settings
steps.requires: The [moving-object workspace](#launch) is open. The site is where the telescope took the images.
actions: Click **Settings** in the top menu bar.
Click **Open Settings**.
steps.check: A settings window opens with a row of tabs across the top.
steps.alt: Settings menu expanded with Settings and Open Settings marked.

steps.title: Enter the telescope coordinates
steps.requires: The [Settings window](#settings-menu) is open. These coordinates come from the example FITS headers.
actions: Click the **Setup** tab. Scroll to **Observing Site** if the fields are below the visible area.
Enter **31.5472** for **Observing Latitude**.
Enter **-99.3825** for **Observing Longitude**. The minus sign indicates west longitude.
Click **Save**. For your own observing night, enter the site where those frames were taken.
steps.check: The settings dialog closes. CAst can now use the example site when checking whether a predicted object was above the horizon.
steps.alt: Setup tab showing latitude 31.5472, longitude −99.3825, and the Save button.

steps.title: Open a folder and inspect it first
steps.requires: The [moving-object workspace](#launch) is open and your image folder is available.
actions: Click **File** in the top left.
Choose **Open Folder**. You can also press **Ctrl+Shift+O**.
steps.check: The folder picker opens. This route lets you choose the reference frame before starting the catalogue search.
steps.alt: File menu expanded with Open Folder outlined.

steps.title: Load a folder and search immediately
steps.requires: The [moving-object workspace](#launch) is open with no source loaded. Set the [observing site](#site) first.
actions: Click the gold **Open** button at the upper left of the workspace.
steps.check: The folder picker opens. With this shortcut CAst starts Generate automatically after you confirm the folder.
steps.alt: The Open workflow button is marked in the empty workspace.

steps.title: Choose the image directory
steps.requires: You opened a folder picker using [File → Open Folder](#open-folder) or the [Open shortcut](#quick-open).
actions: Select **3I practice** for the five-frame walkthrough, or **3I ATLAS full** for the complete 76-frame observation. The **Directory** field should name the extracted folder containing the FITS files.
Click **Choose**. On Windows the native picker may label this button **Select Folder**.
steps.check: The first frame shows a star field. The File menu route leaves **Generate** ready. The gold Open shortcut starts the search, and the object table fills when it finishes.
steps.alt: Directory field showing 3I practice and the Choose button.

steps.title: Open only one solved image
steps.requires: The [moving-object workspace](#launch) is open. A solved image includes a map from pixels to sky coordinates, often called a WCS.
actions: Click **File**.
Click **Open File** or press **Ctrl+O**.
steps.check: A file picker opens. This route is sufficient to identify predicted objects in one exposure. Blink and sequence searches need multiple frames.
steps.alt: File menu with Open File and its Ctrl+O shortcut outlined.

steps.title: Select the first exposure
steps.requires: The [Open File picker](#open-file) is open in either the original folder or your practice folder.
actions: Select **Light_3I_120.0s_Bin1_L_20251207-040231_0001_c.fits**. Check the filename in the field along the bottom.
Click **Open**. Wait while CAst reads the sky coordinates and queries the catalogue over the internet.
steps.check: The first exposure and the predicted-object table appear. If the table stays empty, click **Work Log** and read the last message for a timestamp, sky-coordinate or catalogue error.
steps.alt: File name field showing the first 3I FITS exposure and the Open control.

links.label: Locate the comet in the table

steps.title: Generate known-object predictions
steps.requires: A [folder is loaded](#choose-folder) through the File menu. Use the [example telescope location](#site) and an internet connection.
actions: At the far right of the top row, open **Frame** and choose the entry beginning **1.** and ending **0001_c.fits**. Leave **Group** at **All** for these L / 120 s images.
Click **Generate** at the far left. Keep the window open while CAst queries the catalogue and measures nearby signals.
steps.check: Rows appear in the object table. The first exposure started at 09:00:30 UTC on December 7, 2025. The app uses the FITS timestamp. In this run 50 predictions fell inside the frame. Catalogue updates can change the list.
steps.alt: Frame selector and Generate button marked on the workspace above the first image.

steps.title: Locate 3I/ATLAS in the table
steps.requires: [Generate has finished](#generate) for the first exposure.
actions: Click **3I/ATLAS** in the **Object** column. Scroll within the table if needed.

Click **Inspector** just below the table. Read **Current measured offset** and **Current frame SNR**. Offset is the distance in pixels between the prediction and the nearby peak. SNR tells you how strongly that peak stands out from the local background.
steps.check: The selected row says **Comet** and **interstellar**. The first practice frame gave an offset of 0.33 pixel and SNR 9.82. Check more than one exposure before attributing a peak to the comet.
steps.alt: 3I/ATLAS is selected, and the Inspector lists predicted position, measured offset and frame SNR.

steps.title: Inspect the main-belt asteroid (90) Antiope
steps.requires: [Generate has finished](#generate) on the first exposure.
actions: Click **(90) Antiope** in the object table. Its **Type** is **Asteroid** and its **Class** is **main-belt**.
Click **Inspector**. Compare **Motion rate** with the comet’s 158.41 arcseconds per hour. An arcsecond is a unit of angle on the sky.
steps.check: Antiope moves about 24.8 arcseconds per hour here. It shifts less than 3I/ATLAS between these short practice exposures. The image controls now follow the asteroid you selected.
steps.alt: The selected (90) Antiope row and Inspector tab are marked.

steps.title: Center the selected object
steps.requires: A [comet or asteroid row is selected](#inspect).
actions: Click **Target Marker** if it is off. This draws a marker at the selected position.
Click **Center Object**. Scroll up over the marked position to zoom in further. Click **Target Marker** again when you want a clear view of the underlying pixels.
steps.check: The predicted location is centered in the image. You can now compare that patch across time, or save a marked still.
steps.alt: Image toolbar marks Target Marker and Center Object; a crosshair shows 3I/ATLAS on the actual first frame.

steps.title: Play the frames as a blink
steps.requires: A [folder with at least two images](#choose-folder) is loaded. Select an object row to follow it during playback.
actions: Use **Track Object** to choose your reference. Turn it on to keep the selected prediction centered. Turn it off to keep the registered stars fixed and see the object move.
Click **Blink**. Wait for the first preload to finish. Watch several cycles, then click **Blink** again to pause. If a marker covers the pixels, turn off **Target Marker**.
steps.check: The **Frame** number advances during playback and stops when paused. The practice images share a star grid, so with tracking off the background stays almost fixed.
steps.alt: Track Object and Blink are highlighted above the 3I/ATLAS frame.

steps.title: Compare frame 1 with frame 5
steps.requires: You can use the frame switch on this page immediately. To reproduce the view in CAst, [center 3I/ATLAS](#center), switch off **Track Object** and **Target Marker**, and zoom in over the comet.
actions: Use this page’s **Frame 1** and **Frame 5** controls to switch between captures. In CAst, use the marked **Frame** selector to make the same change.
Watch the diffuse bright patch inside the outlined box. Compare its position with a nearby star outside the box. The zoom and sky position stay fixed between the two images.
steps.check: The comet shifts across the box, while nearby stars stay in approximately the same places. Try toggling several times to see the movement.
steps.alt: First exposure at fixed zoom, with the frame selector and the patch containing the comet marked.

links.label: Measure the motion across all five frames

comparison.label: Frame 5
comparison.alt: Fifth exposure at the same zoom and sky position; the comet has shifted within the marked box.

steps.title: Explore predicted sky motion
steps.requires: [Generate has finished](#generate). This chart shows catalogue positions without the background stars.
actions: Click **Sky View** beneath the object table.
Drag the **Time** slider left or right to move the predictions backward or forward from the observation time.
Click **Now** to return to the exposure time.
steps.check: The time offset returns to UTC +0.0 h. Use [Blink](#blink) to inspect motion recorded in your actual images.
steps.alt: Sky View tab, Time slider, and Now button are marked above the predicted field.

steps.title: Open the trajectory plots
steps.requires: A folder is loaded and an [object is selected](#inspect). Pause Blink if it is running.
actions: Click **Plots** in the top workflow row. Double-clicking the selected object row opens the same charts.
steps.check: A trajectory window opens with position plots, offset and signal-to-noise plots, and a measurement table.
steps.alt: Plots is marked in the top toolbar above the selected comet row.

steps.title: Read the five frame measurements
steps.requires: The [Plots window](#plots-open) is open for 3I/ATLAS.
actions: Click a row in the table to read a single exposure. **Pred x/y** gives the expected pixel position. **Meas x/y** gives the nearby measured peak. Scroll horizontally for **Offset** and **SNR**.
Compare the plotted measured positions with the predicted path above the table. Check the offset plot for a sudden jump to a different source.
steps.check: Here all five frames have measurements and the offsets are approximately 0.3 to 1.1 pixels. Small offsets across several frames support the identification more strongly than a single close match.
steps.alt: All five measurement rows outlined under the trajectory, offset and SNR plots for 3I/ATLAS.

steps.title: Stack the images on the comet
steps.requires: The five-image folder is loaded with [3I/ATLAS selected](#inspect). Close the plots window and stop Blink if needed.
actions: Click **Synthetic Track** in the top row. Use the default object-centered settings for this example. If you enabled advanced settings previously, keep the object-centered crop and the predicted motion.
Wait for the preview. CAst shifts each exposure by the object’s predicted motion before combining them. Light from the moving target adds up in one place.
steps.check: The **Synthetic Tracking** preview opens with a zoomed image, a frame count and the stack measurement.
steps.alt: Synthetic Track button marked above the selected object table.

steps.title: Check the stack and export it
steps.requires: The [Synthetic Tracking preview](#synthetic-open) is open.
actions: Click **Overlays** to choose which marks to display. Compare **Predicted center** with **Measured peak**. Read the used-frame count and the offset above the image.
To keep the stack, click **Export Image…**. Choose **Raw FITS Files** for the numerical stack or **PNG Files** for a rendered preview. Choose a destination, name the file, and click **Save**.
steps.check: The five-frame practice run used 5 of 5 frames, measured a stacked SNR of 6.95 and placed the peak 1.00 pixel from the predicted center. Different settings or frames can change these measurements.
steps.alt: Actual stacked 3I/ATLAS preview with Overlays and Export Image marked.

steps.title: Start a search for additional movers
steps.requires: [Generate has finished](#generate) for your folder. Use at least three solved frames for the default search. Let any blink preload finish.
actions: Click **Discover** in the workflow row. If CAst offers an earlier result, choose **Run New Scan** for a fresh search or **Restore Last Result** to review it.
If the button is disabled, hover over it for the missing requirement. For a mixed folder, select a single filter/exposure group. The practice folder has only one group.
steps.check: For a new search, the **Discover Pipeline** dialog opens. Discover looks for sources whose positions change after the fixed star field is subtracted.
steps.alt: Discover is highlighted in the top controls of the loaded workspace.

steps.title: Run a quick practice scan
steps.requires: The [Discover Pipeline dialog](#discover-open) is open for the five-frame practice folder.
actions: Set **Preset** to **Fast scan**.
Set **Alignment** to **Already aligned**. These example exposures were registered to the same star grid. For a different sequence with drifting stars, choose **Align first**.
Set **Working Binning** to **4x4**. This combines neighboring pixels for a smaller working image.
Clear **If no candidates are found, retry automatically with the detailed full-resolution search** for this short practice scan.
Click **Run Discover**. Leave the progress window open until the batch finishes. If you enabled a final synthetic sweep separately, choose **No** at its prompt to inspect residual-only results.
steps.check: The **Discover Results** window summarizes known objects recovered and additional candidate tracks. Strong binning speeds the exercise and can hide faint or slow movers.
steps.alt: Discover Pipeline with Fast scan, Already aligned, 4x4, the unchecked retry box and Run Discover marked.

steps.title: Read the discovery results
steps.requires: A [Discover scan](#discover-options) has completed, or you restored a previous scan for the same group.
actions: Click **Known Recovered** to see catalogue objects the independent motion search linked across frames. The adjacent **Known Missed** tab lists predictions it did not recover.
Click **Potential Discoveries** to review stronger unmatched tracks. Use the number in parentheses to see whether there are any rows to inspect.
Click **Borderline Review** to see less consistent tracks. Follow up any interesting row by checking its position in the original images across several frames.
steps.check: In this five-frame, 4×4-binned residual scan, zero tracks linked. The 50 catalogue predictions appear under **Known Missed**. The visible-limit benchmark was omitted in this capture, so **Visible Limit** reads **Not estimated**. The separate [first-frame match](#inspect) and [comet stack](#stack-read) still show 3I/ATLAS.
steps.alt: Discovery results with the Known Recovered, Potential Discoveries and Borderline Review tabs marked.

links.label: Check a track in the original images

steps.title: Save a discovery summary
steps.requires: The [Discover Results window](#discover-results) is open.
actions: Click **Export…** in the results window.
Choose **Summary CSV…**. Pick a folder, give the file a name, and click **Save**. Use **Benchmark CSV…** for individual known-object recovery rows or **Candidate Review CSV…** for candidate rows.
steps.check: Open the saved .csv file in a spreadsheet or text editor to review the run outside CAst.
steps.alt: Discovery-results Export menu with Summary CSV highlighted.

links.label: Save an image of the field

steps.title: Export the current image
steps.requires: The [source image](#generate) is open. Select and [center](#center) the object if you want a marked close-up.
actions: Click **Export** on the image toolbar.
Choose **Image…**. The current framing, stretch and visible overlays determine how the exported view looks.
steps.check: A save dialog opens for the rendered image.
steps.alt: Image toolbar Export menu opened with Image highlighted.

links.label: Name the image and save it

steps.title: Name and save the still image
steps.requires: You chose [Export → Image…](#export-image) in the image toolbar.
actions: In the save dialog, choose a destination folder. In **File name** type **3I-ATLAS-frame-01.png**. Leave **PNG Files** selected.
Click **Save**. Open that PNG in your image viewer and compare the visible star field and marker with the app.
steps.check: The saved PNG shows the view you framed. The example image was successfully exported with the selected comet centered.
steps.alt: A PNG filename entered in the save dialog and Save outlined.

steps.title: Export a blink animation
steps.requires: A [sequence](#choose-folder) of at least two frames is loaded. Choose the framing, target marker and tracking state you want to share.
actions: Click **Export** on the image toolbar.
Choose **Blink…**. Select **Animated GIF Files** for a looping image or **MP4 Video Files** for a video. Pick a folder, enter a filename such as **3I-ATLAS-blink.gif**, then click **Save**.
Wait for export to finish. Open the saved file and check that the star field or the tracked target moves as you intended.
steps.check: The five-frame example exported as an animated GIF. A still frame can be saved separately from the same menu.
steps.alt: Export menu with Blink highlighted between Image and Trail.
